experiments.scope: Exact two-round BLAKE3 on64-byte messages with fourteen448-bit-prefix words. Choose m14=t-A and m15=-t-bh mod2^32 to force final round-zero a3=0. 32 prefixes and32 t values each. Seven-way packed evaluator, sparse-set with stale garbage, independent scalar checks of14 edge/initial lane instances per trial, and full digest rehash before returning a projected pair. Twenty-bit event within o0..o3,o5; source reports untrusted212/64 operation counts. Gapped-key extraction at offsets0,36,72,108,144 and pointer-free sparse table at key addresses, descending dense addresses and dummy entries after declined matches; exact same selected digest-bit event. The key search executes a statically lowered 64-register program, independently cross-checked against the scalar reference and readable counting wrapper. The message family remains that of our fixed-a3 submissions.
experiments.hypothesis: The new constrained family has projected birthday behavior near the independent model0.39327. This supports assessing Hfixed but does not establish independence, full-width recovery, or the0.003 allowance.

experiments.scope: The same forced-a3 family, 32 groups of32 messages. A sixteen-bit key (low4 bits of o0,o1,o2,o3) searches a twenty-bit event with four extra bits in o4,o6,o7. Declined matches must write a dummy dense entry to preserve message-number decoding. Same lowered RAM schedule and independent checks. This tests the scaled key-hiding path, not the full160-bit key rare-event bound.
experiments.hypothesis: Projected first-representative recovery remains near the independent comparison model, with a small loss versus storing every event key. This probes table hiding and dummy-entry semantics on fresh seeds without proving Hfixed.
